diagnosis.why: The inserted binding (keep a noun head with any immediately following essential post‑nominal modifier) caused the model to avoid cuts that would split a head+modifier, so it often moved cuts earlier (placing the cut before the noun) to keep the noun+modifier together. That change helps very short pieces and list/title splits (bins ≤3/≤5, best examples) but harms longer, multi‑clause sentences (overall ≤99 negative and a big drop in rank for k=1) by fragmenting adjacent clauses and moving cuts into preceding material.
diagnosis.lesson: When adding a noun‑head+modifier binding, ensure it does not force earlier cuts that fragment adjacent clauses or long spans — only apply it when it can be satisfied without shifting cuts into preceding material.

diagnosis.why: Inserting the fallback made the model avoid splitting noun heads from immediately following post‑nominal modifiers, so cuts that used to fall between head+modifier were instead moved elsewhere (often earlier), producing roughly equal numbers of improvements and degradations and a small net harm concentrated in short/medium pieces (≤5 words). The change therefore traded fixing head+modifier splits for introducing new early cuts that hurt small pieces and enumerations, so overall H_set did not improve.
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should respect that repairing head+modifier splits by preferring cuts after the modifier can push cuts into other short spans or break enumerations, so such a fallback must not force additional early cuts in ≤5-word pieces.
